messages:
rina: Dropping the next round of tweaks for the autoscale control row. Main problem: users skim the card and miss that "Capacity max" can be a burst-only value. We need to rework copy and affordance so it's obvious what will always be there vs what is ephemeral. Screenshot in Figma.

cole: Quick idea: visually separate "Guaranteed" vs "Burst" in the card. Two stacked lines: \"Guaranteed: 2 GPUs\" and below \"Max (with burst): 6 GPUs\". Make the word "Burst" slightly muted and add a tooltip for the phrase. Keeps numbers immediate and clarifies permanence.

viv: I like the two-line pattern. Also propose a subtle dashed outline behind the max number to indicate "soft" capacity. For keyboard users, the tooltip must be focusable and provide the same info.

harry: Implementation detail: dashed backgrounds are doable but can look noisy in dense lists. Alternative: add a tiny "burst" chip next to the max number with secondary color and text "burst"; on hover/focus it expands to a popover with more context + cost delta.

mei: Accessibility: avoid relying on color or dashed strokes alone. The chip should include an explicit text label and aria-describedby linking to the popover content. Also ensure the popover is reachable by keyboard and read by screen readers when opened. Example aria for chip: `aria-label=\"Burst available: adds up to 4 GPUs; press Enter for details\"`.

rina: Good. On copy: replace ambiguous "max" with "Max (may burst)" and add microcopy under numbers: "Guaranteed = always available. Max = peak capacity if spare GPUs exist." Short and explicit.

cole: UX microcopy concern: we need a one-line hover sentence for the popover that explains cost direction: e.g., "Using burst may increase hourly cost by ~20% depending on activity." Also show a small estimated delta when user hovers the popover.

viv: For narrow screens, stacking will take space. Suggest collapsing to a single line: \"2 guaranteed • 6 max (burst)\" and on tap expand into the two-line view. Make sure touch targets are large enough.

harry: Keyboard interactions: chip should toggle the popover with Enter/Space. When popover opens, focus should move to the first focusable element inside (a close button or a learn-more link). On close, focus returns to chip. Avoid trapping focus.

mei: Also recommend a policy link inside the popover labeled "How burst works" with `rel=noopener noreferrer` and ensure the link text is descriptive: "How burst capacity is assigned and billed". This helps screen reader users.

rina: Decision: show "Guaranteed" + "Max (may burst)" as primary lines; add a compact burst chip next to max that opens an accessible popover with cost delta and policy link; on mobile collapse to single-line and expand on tap. Action items: @cole update Figma with dashed-less chip variant, @viv build touch prototype, @mei write aria snippet for the popover, @harry add keyboard flow to the interaction spec.

ui-bot: Noted. Created card AUTOSCALE-889: "Clarify guaranteed vs burst on pool card + accessible popover" and assigned cole, viv, mei, harry.

rina: Thanks all. One last ask: keep the burst label consistent across pool dropdown, pool card, and edit modal. We do not want three different microcopy variants. I'll add a copy-line to the style guide.
